title: Homepage message architecture — three paths (draft)
content:
Objective:
Create three distinct hero/lead messaging directions for the public homepage that map to different buyer intents and funnel flows. Each direction should be actionable as an A/B test, include a short supporting subhead, 2–3 proof points, suggested CTA patterns, and quick measurement plan. Draft copy below is intentionally lean — we will iterate voice once direction is chosen.

Context / constraints:
- Audience is primarily engineers and platform teams evaluating inference runtime and economics. Secondary audience: product managers and engineering leaders who decide vendor relationships.
- Homepage must quickly surface: predictable performance, deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private), and cost control levers — but we must avoid sounding like a feature list.
- Tone should be pragmatic, technical, and trust-building (not hypey).
- Primary CTA in all variants: "Get started" or "See performance". Secondary CTAs: docs, benchmarks, request sales.

Three candidate directions (high-level):

1) Engineering-First: "Deterministic inference for critical paths"
- Hero headline candidates:
  • Deterministic inference for production LLMs
  • Latency you can plan around, not guess at
  • Inference infrastructure you can own without building
- Subhead (single line):
  • A predictable runtime and routing layer that keeps your LLM features fast under real load.
- 3 supporting proof bullets (short):
  • Tailored kernel selection and KV-cache routing to keep p99s stable
  • Dedicated pools and autoscaling that preserve tail latency under burst
  • Per-route tracing + token-level latency breakdowns for debugging
- Suggested CTA pattern: Primary: "See latency benchmarks" — Secondary: "Read runtime docs"
- Best fits: platform engineers, infra buyers evaluating SLAs.
- Measurement: Click-through to benchmarks, time on docs runtime pages, and signups with "dedicated" interest tag.
- Microcopy ideas (below hero):
  • "p99 latency, sequence-aware batching, and fallbacks by policy"
  • Quick link: "How we measure p99 — reproducible test harness" (links to benchmark repo)

2) Economics-Control: "Control inference cost without sacrificing quality"
- Hero headline candidates:
  • Cut inference unit costs without re-training
  • Make your inference spend predictable and measurable
  • Cost controls that don’t break quality
- Subhead (single line):
  • Automated batching, cache recommendations, and quantization profiles tuned for your workload.
- 3 supporting proof bullets:
  • Model/quantization recommendations tied to actual request distributions
  • Intelligent batching + prefix cache to reduce per-token compute
  • Cost-transparent analytics down to token and route levels
- Suggested CTA pattern: Primary: "Estimate savings" — Secondary: "Optimize my workload" (lead form)
- Best fits: growth-stage startups, product teams with cost pressure, finance-savvy buyers.
- Measurement: conversions on estimate tool, demo requests tagged "cost", and reduction in demo-to-contract friction.
- Microcopy: "Save CPU and GPU time with workload-aware quantization recommendations"

3) Reliability-first: "Always-on inference with graceful degradation"
- Hero headline candidates:
  • Keep features live even when load spikes or regions fail
  • Graceful fallbacks and routing so your app never goes dark
  • Redundancy, routing, and versioned rollouts combined into one control plane
- Subhead (single line):
  • Automated model fallbacks, multi-region routing, and canary rollouts that protect availability and user experience.
- 3 supporting proof bullets:
  • Policy-driven fallbacks to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained
  • Canary + A/B rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regression
  • Audit logs and per-request tracing for compliance and postmortem
- Suggested CTA pattern: Primary: "See reliability playbook" — Secondary: "Request an SLA"
- Best fits: enterprise customers, regulated verticals, product owners sensitive to uptime.
- Measurement: downloads of the reliability playbook, SLA/demo requests, and enterprise lead generation.

Differentiation snippets (short bullets to use under any direction):
- "One API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
- "Token-level cost and latency breakdowns for each route"
- "Model catalog with verified performance profiles and quick fallbacks"
- "Smart routing: choose latency, cost, or region as a routing policy"

Competitive angles to call out in microcopy/tests:
- Against big cloud-hosted incumbents: emphasize predictable tail latency and per-request observability rather than only price/scale.
- Against open-source self-hosted stacks: emphasize operational ergonomics, SLA-backed capacity, and single-pane rollout tooling.
- Against single-use inference vendors: emphasize multi-mode deployment parity (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and reproducible benchmarks.

Quick A/B test matrix (week 1–3 experiments):
- Test 1 (Engineering-first vs Economics): hero headline + subhead; primary CTA different (benchmarks vs estimate). Measure CTR and downstream signup attribution.
- Test 2 (Microcopy emphasis): show same headline but toggle microcopy between "p99 stability" vs "cost savings (avg token cost)". Measure time-on-page and docs click.
- Test 3 (Proof formats): use metric-first proof ("p99 = X ms") vs narrative proof (short sentence about mechanism). Measure trust signals (benchmarks click, docs depth).

Copy hygiene and next steps:
- Align final direction with the demo/landing flow: hero CTA should take user to a focused funnel (benchmarks -> sandbox; estimate -> form; playbook -> gated doc with contact).
- Ship two variants for the first week: Engineering-first and Economics-Control (covers two largest segments).
- Ask solutions engineering to prepare 1-page benchmark artifacts (repro harness, test datasets) and a short demo script for both variants.
- Coordinate with growth on events for the "Estimate savings" tool so demo handoff is smooth.

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Which single metric will indicate success for hero copy? (suggested: % of sessions that start the primary funnel for that persona within 3 page views)
- How to present quantization guidance without implying quality loss by default? (need 1–2 short lines on QA/regression monitoring)
- Do we need a separate hero variant for "platform teams evaluating on-prem/air-gapped"? (could be a secondary panel on the same page)

Appendix — one-line alternate headlines to steal from for micro-tests:
- "Predictable tail latency for production LLMs"
- "Turn inference into a predictable cost center"
- "Fall back without losing UX: model routing by policy"
- "One runtime, many deployment modes"

Scratch notes (things to avoid in final):
- Avoid generic words like "best" or broad superlatives without proof.
- Avoid framing as a pure cost-play; many buyers care about latency and reliability first.
- Avoid overloading hero with too many CTAs — pick one primary and 1 subtle secondary.

Contact / owners for next iteration:
- Messaging owner: Priya Kapoor (this doc)
- Benchmarks: Ethan Morales
- Solutions engineering assets: Maya Singh

End of draft — use this as base for copywriter pass and final A/B test plan.
